public_rationale: Gato's launch paper documents the combination Marcus describes: broad abilities in one model, substantial successes and frequent superficial or factually incorrect replies. Support depends on reading novelty as the combined coverage. Earlier multimodal systems already existed. The evidence supports observable unreliability, not a literal claim about an absence of understanding.
limitations: Novelty is scoped to the combination of capabilities.
The qualitative dialogue evidence supplies no overall error rate or measure of comprehension.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: DeepMind's Gato achieves novel cross-modal feats but remains unreliable, mixing brilliance with total discomprehension.

statement.excerpt: DeepMind’s newest star, just unveiled, Gato, is capable of cross-modal feats never seen before in AI, but still, when you look in the fine print, remains stuck in the same land of unreliability, moments of brilliance coupled with absolute discomprehension:
statement.document_title: The New Science of Alt Intelligence

from_speaker: cross-modal feats never seen before in AI
moments of brilliance coupled with absolute discomprehension
our_interpretation: Novelty concerns Gato's combined range of language, vision, game-playing and real robot behavior in one model with shared weights, rather than the first existence of multimodal AI.
Brilliance and discomprehension describe strong performances alongside basic observable failures, rather than measurable mental states.
Just unveiled identifies the launch version and its May 12–14, 2022 public record.
criteria.support_condition: The launch record documents a distinctive combination of modalities and tasks, substantial successful performance, and recurrent basic failures.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable earlier systems already demonstrate the same combined coverage, or launch evaluations rebut the alleged failures and establish reliable performance across the relevant tasks.

evidence.locator: Figure 7 caption, page 10; accompanying results in Sections 4 and 6
evidence.explanation: The launch paper reports one model spanning dialogue, captions, games and real robot control, including human-level or better performance on 23 Atari games, while acknowledging frequent poor dialogue responses. Its prior-work comparison supports novelty in that combined coverage, rather than novelty of multimodality itself.

This earlier model combined speech, image and language tasks. It limits any suggestion that Gato invented multimodal models, but does not establish the same combined coverage of games and real robot control.
